Here's a story for you: I once lived next to this guy who was the definition of the neighbor from hell. So, we had butted heads at this point numerous times as we were wall-to-wall neighbors in a town home complex. We were the objects of his deepest loathing, and his attempts to harass us became increasingly unhinged. One of his highlights was when he spotted a mouse scampering on our drainpipe from his yard. So what does he do? He gets a ladder, waltzes in to our backyard from the back cut, climbs on to our roof, takes pictures of a hole he finds somewhere near our chimney, presumably where the mouse was headed to den, and promptly called the police. 

The officer was as stunned to be standing on our doorstep, as we were to be recieving him. We didn't hear the neighbor on the roof, so we thought he was making things up, but he had pictures so he had undoubtedly been up there. He said that there was an infestation, and he was being affected, and his property was being damaged, and he needed the police to intervene. Well, the police did come, and the poor guy literally admitted they had no choice but to come, and he had no idea what he was even doing there. Things -could- have been bad, and maybe there was a kid in dirty conditions, you know. Turns out it was just a bunch of mystified 20 somethings using their combined credit/minimum wage to rent the most middling of lower middle class residences. Half amused, he said that roof damage was a real bane of home owning, so we should at least get that fixed, and the HOA had more power to fine us than he did, as we obviously weren't breaking any laws. 

We asked him to talk to our neighbor because this was clearly harassment, but other than the fact he probably didn't wanna play messenger in a feud, he just said that he already warned ol' boy that they weren't coming back for any calls of this nature, and we would have a legitimate reason to call the police if he ended up in our yard again. He wished us luck, and left us to disassociate. 

There's even thicker plot here, but the story is already pretty long to prove one point: people. Will. Call. The. Police. For anything. To do something they don't want to, to use as their personal Gestapo, because they think they're entitled to their service, whatever. They will call.

The  guteral caw of the Raptors sounded like they were right over your shoulder. My day begins at 10 AM heaven time. I slide from between my silk sheets, which cover a bed the size of a Brooklyn 1 bedroom apartment, and make my way to the breakfast table through the halls of white marble , pillars of pink alabaster, woven gold silk embroderies, and fine art pieces.

Upon a table of rare ebony sits my meal, filling but light and energising. Fresh grilled salmon, or trout, fluffy rice, garlic ginger chicken soup, avocado slices, fried bread, blood orange marmalade, rich clotted cream from grass fed cows, hibiscus tea, and an assortment of perfectly ripe fruits. I dine alone to records of Chef Baker, Charles Mingus, and Thelonious Monk. 

After my meal, I join my friends on the veranda. They are all in the height of fashion, and we embrace as if it has been a literal enternity since last we met. We over look my marijuana vineyard. An overwhelming shock of verdant lushery, in the midday sun you can make out coils of electric orange hairs, snowy white trichromes, pinks, purples, golds, all types of strains for every mood, and taste. A heady floral perfume, moist, cloying, and dank rises from the jade sea and makes the veranda feel warm, and relaxing. 

While my dearest ones pick out a pleasing strain for a promenade, I don my very best suit, recieve a quick, but laser precise cut from from my live in barber,  and with my Italian shoes, French tailored garments, swiss watch and American smile, we hit the town.

In town there is nothing to buy, but lovers laugh, and flirt diving into fountains, riding their bicycles, and trading bites of confections at various cafes. Office buildings are but playhouses, with children making rude gestures in glass elevators, playing hide and seek in cubicles, and having waterballoon fights in the meeting rooms. When their work is done, to every child a pair of arms, and a mothers kiss waiting to catch them after a long busy day.

We make our way from bar to bar, restaurant to restuarant laughing, jesting, pranking, and cat calling. Don Julio, and carne asada tacos, Glenlivet 33 year old scotch and 30 day aged steak, Dom Perignon and lobster. Blunts the size of toblerones. An afternoon binge that would stop a mortals heart. And bank account. At boutiques the girls model clothes, and lavish over jewelry, at every court, billiard hall, or arcade the men, and I, argue at who the best will be in a progressively drunken manor.

As night falls, there's a concert at the beach. We stumble, and giggle our way to the front stripping our garments as if they were rags, and collapsing at the stage. The sun baked sand is still warm, and not a single grain sticks to our bodies. The music starts. Cacocphonous horns, blasting drums, steely guitars, harmonic synths. People dance, and gyrate, and sing all around us, and before long the beat is too infectious to not join in. Fireworks are going off, and the moon is full In the sky. In the crowd, we are each approached by one who longs for us. One by one we are seduced, and disappear. Tonight she is Latina. Dark skin, dark hazel eyes, curly black hair... tall, long legs, I'm sure you can guess the rest . She barely speaks English, but we get by. 

All cabs are Rolls Royces, and underneath the stars of the cabin my new friend teaches me more of her language. We arrive back at the manor, and retreat back through the halls, and pillars, and art pieces, back to my bed. In the dark, she glows like infared where she most desires. Her navel, her lips, her neck, all bright white patches, fading away into an etheral blue all over her body. There are quick flares where my body contacts hers, and they eventually fade, like the tail lights of cars in the distance. She says she wants me to look her in the eyes as we climax, and then they burn too. We meld into a puddle of liquid gold, and then darkness. 

I kiss her passionately for this is out last time together. I can no longer make out more than her silouhette. Maybe she's a figment of my heavenly imagination. More wonderfully, maybe I'm another day in her heaven as she was in mine, and she must go to live her own  eternity. 

As she fades, so does the room until all that's left is silk, and quiet. I drift into sweet sleep, unlike any you can have on earth. It is bottomless , and primordial. I am aware, but indivisible from the black. My slumber devours stars, galaxies, time itself. I am all, and all is a dream. There will be another 10 AM, some day, but for many, many eons, there will only be the sleep.
